context.title: Thus Shall Babylon Sink
context.summary: God raises a destroying wind against Babylon, the golden cup that made the nations drunk, and names the Medes as attackers; His people are told to flee. Jeremiah sends these words to Babylon with Seraiah, who reads them there, ties the scroll to a stone and throws it into the Euphrates: 'Thus shall Babylon sink.'
context.background: Seraiah, Baruch's brother (compare 32:12), traveled with Zedekiah to Babylon in 594 BC, probably to assure Nebuchadnezzar of Judah's loyalty. Ararat, Minni and Ashchenaz (v. 27) were peoples of the northern mountains around modern Armenia. Verse 64 closes, 'Thus far are the words of Jeremiah,' marking chapter 52 as an appendix.

customs.note: The Hebrew likely means 'quartermaster,' the officer in charge of lodging and supplies on the king's journey.

watchFor: Babylon as 'a golden cup in the Lord's hand' (v. 7), echoed in Revelation 17:4.
The hammering repetition of 'break in pieces' (vv. 20–23).
The sunken scroll (vv. 63–64) is echoed in Revelation 18:21.

people.name: Israel
people.summary: One who follows on another’s heels; supplanter, (Gen. 25:26; 27:36; Hos. 12:2-4), the second born of the twin sons of Isaac by Rebekah. He was born probably at Lahai-roi, when his father was fifty-nine and Abraham one hundred and fifty-nine years old.

people.name: Ashkenaz
people.summary: One of the three sons of Gomer (Gen. 10:3), and founder of one of the tribes of the Japhetic race.

people.name: Nebuchadnezzar
people.summary: In the Babylonian orthography Nabu-kudur-uzur, which means “Nebo, protect the crown!” or the “frontiers.” In an inscription he styles himself “Nebo’s favourite.”

people.name: Jeremiah
people.summary: One of the “greater prophets” of the Old Testament, son of Hilkiah, a priest of Anathoth (Jer. 1:1; 32:6). He was called to the prophetical office when still young (1:6), in the thirteenth year of Josiah (B.C. 628).

people.name: Zedekiah
people.summary: The last king of Judah. He was the third son of Josiah, and his mother’s name was Hamutal, the daughter of Jeremiah of Libnah, and hence he was the brother of Jehoahaz (2 Kings 23:31; 24:17, 18).

people.name: Seraiah
people.summary: The son of Neriah. When Zedekiah made a journey to Babylon to do homage to Nebuchadnezzar, Seraiah had charge of the royal gifts to be presented on that occasion.

places.name: Babylon
places.summary: The Greek form of BABEL; Semitic form Babilu, meaning “The Gate of God.” In the Assyrian tablets it means “The city of the dispersion of the tribes.”

places.name: Zion
places.summary: Sunny; height, one of the eminences on which Jerusalem was built. It was surrounded on all sides, except the north, by deep valleys, that of the Tyropoeon separating it from Moriah, which it surpasses in height by 105 feet.

places.name: Chaldea
places.summary: The southern portion of Babylonia, Lower Mesopotamia, lying chiefly on the right bank of the Euphrates, but commonly used of the whole of the Mesopotamian plain.

places.name: Ararat
places.summary: Sacred land or high land, the name of a country on one of the mountains of which the ark rested after the Flood subsided (Gen. 8:4). The “mountains” mentioned were probably the Kurdish range of South Armenia.

places.name: Ashkenaz
places.summary: One of the three sons of Gomer (Gen. 10:3), and founder of one of the tribes of the Japhetic race.

places.name: Minni
places.summary: Only in Jer. 51:27, as the name of a province in Armenia, which was at this time under the Median kings.

places.name: Jerusalem
places.summary: Called also Salem, Ariel, Jebus, the “city of God,” the “holy city;” by the modern Arabs el-Khuds, meaning “the holy;” once “the city of Judah” (2 Chr. 25:28).

places.name: Euphrates
places.summary: Hebrew, Perath; Assyrian, Purat; Persian cuneiform, Ufratush, whence Greek Euphrates, meaning “sweet water.” The Assyrian name means “the stream,” or “the great stream.”

events.title: Prophecies of Jeremiah
events.summary: Passage: Jeremiah 1:1–52:34. People: Jeremiah. Lasted about 67 years.
